carousel.note: Invented phases of a cabinet-making project.

phases.title: Measure the alcove
phases.text: Three heights and three widths; the wall is out of true by 6 mm.

phases.title: Cut the carcass
phases.text: 18 mm birch ply, nested on two sheets with 4 mm kerf.

phases.title: Dry fit
phases.text: Dominos in every joint, clamped without glue for a day.

phases.title: Glue up
phases.text: Two people, one open time of twelve minutes.

phases.title: Hang the doors
phases.text: Concealed hinges, 2 mm reveal all round.

phases.title: Oil the fronts
phases.text: Two coats, a day apart, rubbed back between.

phases.title: Fit and scribe
phases.text: Scribe the end panel to the wall with a compass.

sections.title: Opening the studio
body: Switch the vent fan on before anything else, then check the kiln room is above 10 °C: cold shelves crack.
Read yesterday's firing log and note any cone that bent short.

sections.title: Mixing glazes
body: Weigh dry materials to the gram, add water to a cream consistency and sieve twice.
Label every bucket with the recipe, the date and your initials.

sections.title: Loading the kiln
body: Wipe glaze off every foot. Leave a finger's width between pots and keep the cone pack visible from the spy hole.
Load heavy pieces low and the thin porcelain on the top shelf.

sections.title: Firing and cooling
body: Fire on the medium-speed schedule to cone 6 with a ten-minute hold, then let it cool closed.
Open below 100 °C. Crackle in a celadon keeps forming for days; that is the glaze, not a fault.

sections.title: overview.md
lines: Six repairers, one hall, the first Saturday of every month from October.
The season runs in four stages: prepare the hall, find the repairers, run the first night and look back.

sections.title: budget.csv
lines: Hall hire: 40 per night. Tea and biscuits: 12. Parts fund: whatever the raffle jar holds.
The season is planned to cost 312 across six nights, paid from the co-op account.

sections.title: rota.csv
lines: Door: Lena, then Tomasz. Electrics: Ravi. Bikes: Marcus and Anya. Sewing: Odile. Tea: whoever arrives first.
Swaps are agreed in the group chat and written here the same night.

sections.title: house-rules.md
lines: Show, do not take over. Test anything mains-powered before it leaves. Turn away gas and medical equipment kindly.
The full clauses are drafted as numbered rules in the margin-notes layout.

sections.title: closing-checklist.sh
lines: Wipe the benches. Count the log. Return the urn washed. Lock the side door, then the front.
Photograph the whiteboard before it is wiped.

sections.title: meeting-notes.md
lines: 5 Oct: agreed one item each when more than twelve are waiting.
19 Oct: Odile confirmed for sewing; the second bike stand is still to be found.

sections.title: Doors and sign-in
sections.intro: How people arrive, wait and are looked after.

clauses.title: Doors open at six
clauses.text: The hall is opened by the lead repairer at six and visitors may enter from then. No item is accepted after eight forty.

answer.label: Option a
answer.text: Six, as in the old hall.

clauses.title: One item each on a full night
clauses.text: When more than twelve people are waiting, each visitor may bring one item to the bench until the queue clears.

sections.title: At the bench
sections.intro: What repairers do and do not do.

clauses.title: Show, do not take over
clauses.text: A repairer explains each step and lets the owner hold the tool wherever it is safe to do so.

answer.label: Agreed
answer.text: This is the point of the night.

history.text: Draft said repairers should finish the job; changed after the first meeting.
Wording about holding the tool added.

clauses.title: Mains items are tested before they leave
clauses.text: Any lamp or appliance that was opened is tested at the electrical bench, and the result is written in the log.

answer.label: Option b
answer.text: Two people sign the log line.

clauses.title: No repairs on gas or medical equipment
clauses.text: Gas appliances, heaters with a pilot light and anything used for care are turned away with a kind word and a suggestion of who to ask.

sections.title: Closing
sections.intro: Leaving the hall as we found it.

clauses.title: The log is counted before the lights go off
clauses.text: Items looked at, fixed and not fixed are added up by the door counter and written on the whiteboard photo.

history.text: Door counter added to the kit list.

review.note: Invented review cases for 0.2: notes pinned to quoted words, with a suggestion where there is one.

cases.label: Contract review
cases.context: A tenant's reviewer reads clause 2 of an invented tenancy before it is signed.

sections.title: Tenant's covenants
sections.intro: The Tenant agrees with the Landlord:

clauses.text: to pay the Rent on the due date without deduction;
to pay interest at 10% per month on Rent unpaid for 14 days;

notes.title: Interest of 10% per month
notes.body: That is about 120% a year, likely unenforceable as a penalty; per annum was probably meant.

clauses.text: to yield up the Premises on ____________ in good repair.

notes.title: The hand-back date is blank
notes.body: Without it the tenancy has no end date to hold the tenant to.

cases.label: Privacy notice
cases.context: A data-protection officer reviews a shop's draft privacy notice before it is published.

sections.title: How long we keep your data

clauses.text: We keep your order history for as long as necessary and may share it with selected partners.

notes.title: “As long as necessary” is not a period
notes.body: The notice must say how long, or how the period is decided.

notes.title: Which partners?
notes.body: Name the kinds of partner and why they get the data.
notes.suggestion: our delivery partners, to deliver your orders

clauses.text: You can ask for a copy of your data by writing to us.

notes.title: Offer email too
notes.body: Writing by post only makes the right harder to use than it should be.
notes.suggestion: by writing to us or emailing privacy@shop.example

cases.label: Peer review of a paper
cases.context: A reviewer annotates the abstract of an invented study before sending it back to the authors.

clauses.text: In a survey of 12 cafés, those with outdoor seating sold more cold drinks. This proves that outdoor seating causes higher drink sales.

notes.title: An observation cannot prove a cause
notes.body: The survey shows a link; the weather, the street or the menu could explain it.
notes.suggestion: suggests that outdoor seating is linked to

notes.title: Twelve cafés is a small sample
notes.body: Say so in the abstract, or widen the survey.

cases.label: Release note
cases.context: A support lead checks a release note before it goes to customers. One note was already judged not a problem.

clauses.text: Exports are now faster. The legacy API has been removed. Contact support if anything breaks.

notes.title: Removing an API needs a date and a path
notes.body: Customers on the legacy API need to know when it stops and what to move to.
notes.quote: The legacy API has been removed.
notes.suggestion: The legacy API stops on 1 March; move to the v2 API (see the migration guide).

notes.title: “Faster” by how much?
notes.body: A number would make the claim checkable.

stack.note: Invented: the plan for a repair-cafe season, four stacked sections. The third is taller than the screen.

sections.title: Fix it together, first Saturday of the month
text: People bring a broken lamp, a flat bike, a coat with a split seam. Someone who knows how sits with them and shows how to fix it.
Nothing is mended for them while they watch the clock. That is the whole idea, and it is why the evening works.

sections.title: Six repairers and a desk
text: Two for bikes, two for lamps and small electrics, one for sewing and one on the door.
Each repairer brings their own tools. The co-op supplies the benches, the light and the tea.

sections.title: The long list, bench by bench
text: Everything below has an owner by the end of the month. This section is taller than the screen on purpose: it sticks when its bottom meets the bottom of the screen, so all of it can be read before the next one covers it.

list.name: Floor tape
list.text: Marks where visitors wait so the benches stay clear.

list.name: Parts bins
list.text: Sorted by size: screws, washers, fuses, bulbs, plugs.

list.name: Lamp tester
list.text: One mains tester at the electrical bench, checked every night.

list.name: Bike stand
list.text: Two stands, one for kids' bikes.

list.name: Tea urn
list.text: Borrowed from the church hall; return it washed.

list.name: Repair log
list.text: One sheet per item: what, who, fixed or not.

list.name: Sign-in desk
list.text: A table by the door with a pen on a string.

list.name: First-aid kit
list.text: Checked before each night, restocked from the petty cash.

list.name: Spare fuses
list.text: 3 A, 5 A and 13 A, in a labelled tin.

list.name: Soldering mat
list.text: Heat-proof, kept on the electrical bench only.

list.name: Needle tin
list.text: Sewing needles counted in and out.

list.name: Glue shelf
list.text: Contact glue stays on the top shelf, away from the tea.

list.name: Extension leads
list.text: Six, tagged with the date they were last tested.

list.name: Cable ties
list.text: A jar of black and a jar of white.

list.name: Torches
list.text: Two, for looking inside things.

list.name: Waste box
list.text: Beyond repair goes to the recycling run on Sunday.

list.name: Raffle jar
list.text: Coins for the parts fund; empty it on the way out.

list.name: Coat rack
list.text: Visitors' coats go here, not on the benches.

list.name: Magnifier lamp
list.text: Shared between sewing and electrics.

list.name: Whiteboard
list.text: Tonight's repairers and what they can fix.

list.name: Photo release
list.text: Ask before photographing anyone's repair.

list.name: Quiet corner
list.text: For people waiting on a long repair.

list.name: Door counter
list.text: A click counter for the evening's visitors.

list.name: Lost property
list.text: A box. Anything left is kept for a month.

sections.title: Doors at six, last repair at nine
text: Visitors sign in, wait for a free bench and leave with their item mended or with a plain answer about why it cannot be.
At nine the benches are wiped, the log is counted and the tea urn goes back to the church hall.
